Can I just say that airports are the most stressful places on earth? You'd think we'd have figured out how to make the experience less awful, but nope. You still gotta show up two hours early, take your shoes off for strangers, and sit in a chair designed by someone who hates comfort.

But here's the flip side: actually being somewhere new? That part's amazing. There's this thing that happens when you step out of an airport in a different country and everything smells different and looks different and you can't read the signs. It's scary but also the best feeling ever?

I'm a big fan of just wandering with no plan. Guidebooks are fine, but the best stuff happens when you're lost. You turn down some random street and find this incredible little restaurant that's not on any list, and the person running it doesn't speak your language but they're so nice, and the food is unreal.

Travel's one of those things where the memories get better over time. Even the disasters turn into great stories eventually. "Remember when we missed the train and had to sleep in that bus station?" Terrible at the time. Hilarious now.
